memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then he and the men who were with him ate and drank and spent the night there. When they got up the next morning, he said, 'Send me on my way to my master.' But her brother and her mother replied, 'Let the young woman remain with us ten days or so; then you may go.' But he said to them, 'Do not detain me, now that the LORD has granted success to my journey. Send me on my way so I may go to my master.'" - Gen 24:54-56 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
With the mission accomplished, the servant is eager to return. Rebekah's family, understandably, wants a little more time with her — ten days or so. But the servant gently insists: "Do not detain me, now that the LORD has granted success to my journey."

There is a lesson here about not lingering once God has made the way clear. The family's request was not sinful; it was natural affection. Yet good things can sometimes slow us down from doing what God has called us to do. The servant kept his focus on completing his task and returning to his master.

We can face similar delays. Once God has shown us the way forward, all sorts of reasonable requests and comfortable reasons can tempt us to postpone obedience. "Just a little longer" can quietly become months and years.

When the Lord has granted success and made the path plain, there is wisdom in moving promptly. Obedience delayed can drift into obedience denied. Ask God for the servant's steady focus — the resolve to finish what has been started and not be held back from where God is sending you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What good things might be slowing my obedience to God?
2. Where is "just a little longer" delaying what God has made clear?
3. Do I finish the tasks God gives me, or leave them incomplete?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me focused on finishing what You have called me to do. Do not let even good things hold me back from prompt obedience. Amen.
